CYTOGENETICS AND MOLECULAR CYTOGENETICS REPORT
[redacted name] Medical Center
Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient: [redacted name]
Age: 25 years
MRN: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Bone marrow aspirate
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
New diagnosis of acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL)

TESTS PERFORMED
1. Conventional Cytogenetics (Karyotype Analysis)
2. Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH) Panel:
   - BCR/ABL1 dual color dual fusion probe
   - KMT2A (MLL) break-apart probe
   - Deletion 5q probe set (EGR1/D5S23,D5S271)

RESULTS

KARYOTYPE ANALYSIS
Method: G-banding analysis performed on 20 metaphase cells from 24-hour and 48-hour unstimulated bone marrow cultures

Result: 46,XY,t(9;22)(q34;q11.2)[8]/46,XY,t(9;22)(q34;q11.2),add(5)(q31)[4]/46,XY[8]

ABNORMAL KARYOTYPE DETECTED
- Primary clone: t(9;22)(q34;q11.2) in 8/20 cells (40%)
- Sideline clone: t(9;22)(q34;q11.2) with additional material on 5q31 in 4/20 cells (20%)
- Normal male karyotype in 8/20 cells (40%)

FLUORESCENCE IN SITU HYBRIDIZATION (FISH)

1. BCR/ABL1 (Vysis LSI BCR/ABL Dual Color, Dual Fusion Translocation Probe)
Result: nuc ish(ABL1x3,BCRx1)(ABL1 con BCRx1)[186/200]
ABNORMAL - BCR/ABL1 rearrangement detected in 93% of interphase nuclei
Variant signal pattern observed: 1 fusion, 2 red (ABL1), 1 green (BCR) - consistent with loss of 3'BCR region

2. KMT2A Break-Apart Probe (11q23)
Result: nuc ish(5'KMT2A,3'KMT2Ax2)[200]
NORMAL - No KMT2A rearrangement detected
200/200 nuclei with normal 2 fusion signal pattern

3. Deletion 5q Probe Set (EGR1/D5S23,D5S271)
Result: nuc ish(EGR1,D5S23,D5S271)x2[200]
NORMAL - No deletion of 5q detected
200/200 nuclei with normal signal pattern for all probes

INTEGRATED INTERPRETATION
The cytogenetic and FISH findings demonstrate:

1. Philadelphia chromosome t(9;22)(q34;q11.2) resulting in BCR-ABL1 fusion, detected by both karyotype and FISH analysis. The FISH variant pattern with loss of 3'BCR sequences is a known variant that does not affect the clinical significance.

2. Clonal evolution with acquisition of additional material on chromosome 5q31 in a subset of Philadelphia-positive cells, suggesting disease progression.

3. No involvement of KMT2A (MLL) gene or deletion of 5q, excluding these as additional abnormalities.

DIAGNOSIS
B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with t(9;22)(q34;q11.2); BCR-ABL1
(WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues, 2016)

CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE
The presence of t(9;22)/BCR-ABL1 defines a specific entity in the WHO classification with distinct therapeutic and prognostic implications. This tyrosine kinase activating abnormality is targetable with tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs). The presence of clonal evolution at diagnosis may indicate a more aggressive disease course. The high percentage of BCR-ABL1 positive cells (93%) confirms active disease.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Reviewed by: [redacted name], MD, PhD
